protocol.baseline_overflow_scope: Rust release sum wraps outside its representable result range; all timed/successful probe sizes are <=1048576, so u64 overflow is impossible there. Huge probes force allocation refusal. The HIA proof retains checked semantics beyond this measurement profile.
claims_limits: one shared Linux x86_64 host; affinity is not exclusive CPU ownership
Rust byte arm receives the same modular arithmetic simplification explicitly
guard is machine-range-based and executed; benchmark lengths are not proof assumptions
p95/p99 are batch latencies, not per-invocation tail latencies
native compiler/linker/libc/hardware remain trusted; no backend refinement theorem
manual engineering, historical tool acquisition and energy costs are unknown
protocol.order: rotate all four arms by seed index, reverse odd rotations; retain every sample and predeclared gate
protocol.registration: both workload sources and all lengths frozen before campaign; affine is a second arithmetic/load shape, not an independent production application
protocol.semantics: fallible zero-initialized owned bytes, explicit wrapping fill, checked u64 reduction, release; refusal returns 1001
protocol.source_profile: Rust 1.95.0 actual identity; Clang 20+ actual identity; generic x86_64; no target-cpu=native
